strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing physical plausibility in 3D compositional scene generation for robotic simulation
Creative reformulation of composition as collision-aware registration problem using spatial priors from generated scenes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple baselines, quantitative metrics, and extensive qualitative results
Training-free approach generalizes better than learning-based baselines without requiring large training datasets
Valuable dataset contribution of ~8,300 interactive 3D scenes to be released
Honest documentation of failure cases and clear identification of limitations
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—primarily a well-motivated combination of existing techniques (OBB, GeoTransformer, ICP, SDF) rather than novel methods
Heavy dependence on external proprietary models and services (Nano Banana Pro, TRELLIS2, PartField, GeoTransformer, Gemini VLM) compromises reproducibility claims
Quantitative evaluation limited to only 10 test cases; no user studies or perceptual evaluation of semantic correctness
Missing validation on actual robotic manipulation tasks despite strong robotic simulation motivation
No comparison with most related recent work (COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE using VLM-guided composition)
Scalability concerns: sequential composition for multi-object scenes may accumulate errors; only demonstrated up to 5 objects
Agentic refinement underspecified regarding convergence, computational cost, and success rates
Critical ablation studies missing: removing Stage 2, varying β(k) schedule, comparing registration methods
Failure modes (symmetry ambiguity, occlusion propagation, fine-grained components) acknowledged but not solved; proposed solutions are future work
Dataset validation limited: no inter-observer metrics, composition diversity analysis, or quality assessment of physical plausibility

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap: existing 3D generation produces fused geometry lacking object-object spatial relationships, which is critical for robotic simulation
Comprehensive and thoughtful two-stage composition pipeline combining global-to-local registration with SDF-based collision-aware optimization, with principled β(k) scheduling
Creative agentic refinement strategy using VLM-based semantic-level correction to handle severe geometric mismatches from 2D occlusions that rigid transformation alone cannot fix

Extensive empirical validation: 150 test cases with quantitative metrics (CLIP, human/VLM ratings, geometric intersection), ablation study showing component contributions, and 140+ supplementary results
Significant dataset contribution: ~8,300 compositional 3D scenes across 9 categories with flexible reference meshes
Clear, well-structured presentation with effective figures demonstrating pipeline design and qualitative superiority over baselines
Training-free approach avoiding large-scale data requirements; works with both manually-modeled and generated assets
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines established techniques (OBB, GeoTransformer, scale-aware ICP, SDF optimization) without significant algorithmic innovation

Critical reproducibility issues: heavy dependence on closed-source proprietary tools (Nano Banana Pro for image generation, Gemini 3 Pro for VLM refinement, TRELLIS2 for 3D reconstruction), severely limiting reproducibility despite promised code release

Incomplete physical validity evaluation: geometric intersection metrics (Eqs. 4-5) only measure spatial overlap, not true physical plausibility; no validation in actual physics engines (PyBullet, PhysX); ignores mass, friction, center-of-mass factors critical for robotic applications

Insufficient analysis of spatial guidance quality: method relies on PartField-segmented meshes acknowledged to contain 'holes and geometric artifacts', but robustness to these artifacts lacks empirical validation; no sensitivity analysis on guidance quality impact

Dataset construction unclear: selection criterion from ~10,000 to ~8,300 candidates not specified; dataset generation process unspecified (same pipeline?); missing quality metrics, inter-annotator agreement, bias analysis

Agentic refinement under-analyzed: max 5 iterations appears arbitrary without justification; no analysis of convergence, iteration distribution, or failure modes; success entirely dependent on VLM quality

Scalability concerns with sequential composition: multi-part scenes require N-1 pipeline passes for N objects with potential error accumulation; no computational cost analysis or timing information provided

Evaluation limitations: only 150 test cases for quantitative evaluation (relatively small); ~2.3% failure rate on edge cases (Figure 7, 9) without proposed mitigation strategies; no physics simulator validation
Limited scope: declared limitation to 'daily objects'; most test cases appear relatively simple; applicability to complex robotic scenarios or fine-grained components (screws, tight joints) unclear

Hyperparameter choices lack justification: λ=0.003, kmax=100, βmax=3.0, max iterations=5 appear empirically chosen; claimed robustness 'within reasonable range' without sensitivity analysis or ablation studies
Potential biases in evaluation: VLM ratings (Qwen3) used as metric without demonstrating consistency with human ratings; missing comparisons with other optimization-based composition baselines
Methodological gap: method relies on PartField guidance containing acknowledged artifacts—mechanism for robustness unexplained; no analysis of complete PartField failures
